output.why:
E has the most controlled voice of the six. It gives the reader the piano, the nocturne, the unsurprised Aurèle, and Odile never asking where he had been, and it withholds everything it can. Its ending, "I have no more to add," is spare, and the request about Félix and the newspapers lands harder for it. Its one flourish, "out in the frost," is earned.

A has the cleanest clockwork: each timestamp is set down once and the repeater's chimes are described exactly. Its final paragraph turns the watch into the confession's last move ("Everything else I told you is true"), which is the best structural idea in the set. The ending, "Please tell Odile before the others do," is restrained and practical. Its weakness is a slightly administrative tone in places.

D has the best individual sentences: "The room was full of that sound, and then it was not," and "I could not have stopped myself." The middle of the letter carries the crime clearly. Its closing Latin tag is cute and works against the restraint elsewhere, though "I find I mean it too" is strong.

C has a confident, believable voice and a strong last line ("Each year at dinner he told me my watch ran fast. It did."). It explains a little more than it needs to, though, in "I should have reckoned on the house. A house of this kind keeps its own time," and the watch and clock logic is spelled out more than the others.

F has the most thoughtful idea, that the town agrees about time and the repeater cannot be made to unsay what it has said. That idea runs into lecture, though: the Temple sermon, the Latin tags, the grammar joke. The timeline is also less legible, with no stepwise movements. Its ending ("shall not need to be fetched") is good.

B is the weakest. It moralises ("I have been a careful physician, which is a different thing and a worse one"), tacks on subplots (Félix's father's letter, Girard, Félix's brandy) that the confession has no need of, and leans on Tempora mutantur. It explains its own clockwork and its own guilt, so the reader is told what to feel. Its ending ("I have no claim left to make") is a fair line buried in too much argument.
